name: Lateral anterolateral approach to the distal femur (periprosthetic knee)
corridor: Lateral incision from Gerdy tubercle along the mid-lateral femur, IT-band split, distal-to-proximal vastus-lateralis elevation, and optional lateral arthrotomy to the tibial component, safe beside a healed midline TKA scar

positioning.text: Position supine so the lateral condyle, Gerdy tubercle, and femoral shaft can be imaged; this corridor is safe next to a healed midline TKA scar.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark Gerdy tubercle, the lateral femoral condyle, the mid-lateral femoral shaft, and the prior midline scar.

incision.text: Begin in the mid-lateral femoral line at Gerdy tubercle and curve proximally over the lateral condyle as far as the fracture requires. Carry it distal to Gerdy only if an arthrotomy is needed.

superficial_interval.text: Divide the IT band once, in line with its fibers, including the distal slope toward Gerdy tubercle.

deep_interval.text: Incise vastus-lateralis fascia just anterior to the lateral intermuscular septum and elevate the muscle from distal to proximal. Ligate profunda perforators. Optional arthrotomy over the anterior third of the lateral condyle can reach the lateral tibial component.

layers.text: Skin, IT band, vastus lateralis and septum, periosteum, optional lateral capsule, then the distal femur.

structures_at_risk.text: Lateral genicular vessels, profunda perforators, periosteum, the patellar tendon, and the posterior popliteal neurovascular bundle if dissection strays behind the septum are at risk.

danger_zones.text: Uncontrolled posterior dissection toward the popliteal vessels is the danger zone. Failure to ligate perforators causes heavy bleeding.

retraction_hazards.text: Avoid excessive tension on the patellar tendon during arthrotomy, especially in osteoporotic bone.

exposure.text: Shows the lateral distal femur for reduction and plating, with optional joint view as far as the lateral tibial component.

limitations.text: There are no major named nerves on the lateral knee, but the window does not expose the medial femur. Arthrotomy is optional.

indications.text: Used to visualize, reduce, and fix a distal-femoral periprosthetic fracture beside a healed midline TKA incision.

closure.text: Close any arthrotomy, vastus fascia, and IT band with absorbable suture, then close skin routinely.

complications.text: Complications include perforator bleeding, patellar-tendon injury, periosteal stripping that delays union, and popliteal neurovascular injury from posterior dissection.

procedure_applications.condition: A distal-femoral periprosthetic fracture is reduced and plated laterally beside a healed TKA incision

questions.question: Is this approach safe next to a healed midline TKA scar?
How far can the optional arthrotomy be carried?
questions.answer: Distally as far as the lateral tibial component.

questions.question: Which vessels must be ligated during vastus elevation?
